correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed the exact rank-two base-polytope H-description from parallel classes: x_e>=0, x(C_j)<=1 and x(E)=2; p=2 has both class sums identically 1. Reflection -(P-c) subset s(P-c) is equivalent to (s+1)c-v in sP for every base vertex. For p>=3 the coordinate maximum=1 and each class minimum=0 give necessary/sufficient (s+1)c_e>=1, (s+1)c(C_j)<=s. With w=(s+1)c the feasible class masses range [m_j,s] and total 2(s+1), yielding exactly s=max(max m_j,(n-2)/2,2/(p-2)). Nonnegative residual z=w-1 with caps q_j=s-m_j and total Z=2(s+1)-n proves the full center-polytope and the three affine-dimension regimes (Z=0; Z=U>0; 0<Z<U). The p=2 direct-product exception gives s=max(1,m1-1,m2-1) and the product-of-simplices center dimension. Independently solved a linear program from facet constraints for seven distinct parallel profiles, all matching the exact formula. The proof covers all positive integral class sizes, not by finite extrapolation.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2024 robust optimization LP covers *computing* Minkowski centers for arbitrary polyhedra but does not supply the rank-two closed value and all affine-dimension cases without substantive specialized elimination. The independence-polytope theorem includes 0 and is full-dimensional, whereas a base polytope satisfies x(E)=2. They are not the same object; the latter may be recovered as a face, but Minkowski asymmetry of faces is not determined by that of the original polytope.

originality.rationale: PASS best-of-knowledge: Ferroni-Jochemko-Schroeter determine the relevant parallel class rank-two matroid base-polytope facets and Ehrhart data, but not their affine Minkowski asymmetry or all centers. Den Hertog-Pauphilet-Soali Proposition 4 gives a general robust polyhedral LP, which can recover each case after specialized analysis but does not itself evaluate the three competing obstructions, p=2 product exception, or dimension stratification. A published same-invariant record for polymatroid *independence* polytopes expressly excludes matroid *base* polytopes with x(E)=rank: its density-tight criterion does not imply this formula. Distinct Euclidean inradius rank-two results do not transfer to affine-invariant asymmetry. The closed classification and center-locus cases survive these implication tests.

value.rationale: PASS: Exact asymmetry for all loopless rank-two matroids with arbitrary parallel classes is a natural complete matroid-polytope classification; three sharp obstructions, a disconnected p=2 exception and the whole possibly-positive-dimensional minimizing-center locus distinguish qualitatively different regimes. The cap-residual geometry and dimension criterion are reusable structural data not given by a generic numerical optimization method. Even if an arbitrary instance could be solved by LP, the quantified symbolic family and exact strata are meaningful.

limitations: Finite, loopless rank-two matroids only, intrinsically in the affine hull; no extension to arbitrary rank.
General Minkowski-center LP is prior, so originality is the explicit symbolic rank-two evaluation and complete center dimensions, not the reflection definition.
